text:
Sam: FYI nightly eval triggered a sharp regression after onboarding model v2.1.0 this morning. eval-bot found a 12-point hit on the 'customer-support' prompt set. attaching quick summary from the run.

eval-bot: Nightly eval 2026-03-18 06:00Z — model:redwood/v2.1.0 — metric: avg_exact_match dropped from 78.4 -> 66.1 on promptset: customer-support. Alerts: quality_regression.

Priya: Oof. Any failing examples? can we repro locally?

Sam: Pasted two representative failures below — these were fine on v2.0.8 but now truncated/incorrect: 
1) Input: "User: How do I reset my password?"
   v2.0.8: "You can reset your password from Settings > Security — click 'Reset password' and follow the email link."
   v2.1.0: "You can reset your password from Settings >" (stops).
2) Input: "Customer: Refund policy for annual plan?"
   v2.0.8: correct policy blurb 
   v2.1.0: hallucinated dates + wrong currency.

Miguel: Interesting — truncation and hallucination together suggests either tokenizer change or KV cache misalignment. Did the tokenizer version change with this release?

Jin: Yes — packaging notes on the model repo say tokenizer v3.0.0 was rolled in to support new BPE merges. That could change token ids/prefix lengths.

Priya: I pulled tokenization diffs for the failing inputs. Sample: 
```
# input: "How do I reset my password?"
old_tokens: [121, 34, 50256]
new_tokens: [121, 34, 21, 50256]
# new inserted token id 21 mid-sentence -> changes sequence length and kv offsets
```
This extra token pushes past our configured max_seq in the canary runtime which triggers early stopping in the runtime.

Miguel: That lines up. Also saw this in logs: `runtime: decoded_length > kv_cache_capacity, dropping tail`. ops-bot captured the runtime warn on one of the canaries.

ops-bot: warn: canary-instance-5 — kv cache overflow detected for model redwood/v2.1.0 during batch 4821.

Sam: Did we change default max_seq in the model artifact? I thought we kept the same.

Jin: No explicit change, but the tokenizer introduced a new BOS token mapping that increased typical tokenized length by ~8% on our customer prompt set. No model-graph changes.

Priya: Aside from token length, I ran quick quantization sanity checks — v2.1.0 was shipped with a 4-bit qweight profile (Q4_0) vs v2.0.8 that used Q8_0 on the commit we evaluated. Sample diffs show small logit shifts but not enough alone to cause truncation. So root cause looks like tokenization + overflow interaction.

Miguel: Good catch. We should separate fixes: 1) pin tokenizer to v2.0.2 in the runtime, 2) increase kv cache capacity (fast but costs perf), 3) re-run nightly eval with both changes.

Jin: Quick repro steps I used: 
```
# reproduce locally
rlwrap python -m redwood.inference.cli --model redwood/v2.1.0 --prompt-file samples/customer_qa.txt --max-tokens 128
# inspect tokens
python -c "from tok import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer('v3.0.0'); print(t.encode('How do I reset my password?'))"
```
That showed the extra token.

Sam: Let's prioritize a hotfix canary that pins tokenizer back and keeps v2.1.0 weights. Who can open the rollout?

Priya: I can open a rollback-pr on the packaging repo to pin tokenizer to v2.0.2 and publish a patched artifact as v2.1.0-patch1. Will also add a test to the onboarding pipeline asserting tokenized lengths don't jump >5% vs baseline for our core promptsets.

Miguel: I'll provision a canary with increased kv cache (x1.5) and run eval-bot's nightly job manually against it. If results look normal, we can rollout patch to canary traffic (5%) then ramp.

Jin: One other gotcha — downstream SDKs that used `tokenizer.decode(..., skip_special_tokens=True)` may behave differently if token ids changed; add compatibility note in release notes.

Sam: Agreed. Also track quantization follow-up: Priya, can you run a small A/B of Q4 vs Q8 on a subset to estimate quality delta? we should be explicit about tradeoffs in the PR.

Priya: Yep — I'll run 2k prompts across the customer-support + billing sets and post BLEU/ROUGE and a small human spot-check report. My hypothesis: Q4 is fine for most, but combined with tokenization length changes it amplified instability in end-of-sequence behavior.

eval-bot: Manual eval run queued by Miguel on canary-instance-9.

Sam: Timeline: patch PR by EOB today, canary eval in ~2 hours, manual rollback plan if canary fails. I'll notify support to mute alerts for the spurious failures (we'll reopen after canary). @Priya @Miguel @Jin please post updates here.

Miguel: Update 07:45Z — canary run completed, avg_exact_match on customer-support recovered to 77.9 on patched artifact (within noise). Uploading diffs to the run bucket: https://s3.redwood-infra/internal-evals/2026-03-18/canary-run-171069

Priya: Patch merged and artifact published as redwood/v2.1.0-patch1. Added tokenizer pin and token-length check. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/model-packaging/pulls/432

Sam: Nice. Closing loop: follow-up tasks — (1) add tokenizer-change gating to onboarding checklist, (2) add a regression test that simulates kv cache edge-case with +10% tokenization length, (3) schedule a QA pass for quantization profiles. I'll add in Jira.

Jin: Also recommend we publish a short compatibility note for customers about minor tokenizer changes and how to pin to older tokenizer if they self-host.

Sam: Thanks team — great triage. :thumbsup:
